'''Nivarthi Suryanarayanashastry Satya Murthy''' (5 February 1936 – 8 October 1984) was an Indian physicist and the head of the Nuclear Physics Division of the [[Bhabha Atomic Research Centre]]. Known for his research in molecular [[reaction dynamics]], Murthy was an elected fellow of the [[Indian National Science Academy]], [[National Academy of Sciences, India]] and [[Indian Academy of Sciences]]. The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]], the apex agency of the [[Government of India]] for scientific research, awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]], one of the highest Indian science awards,<ref name="SHANTI SWARUP BHATNAGAR AWARD FOR GENOMICS AND MOLECULAR WORK IN PULSES">{{Cite web|url=http://www.icrisat.org/shanti-swarup-bhatnagar-award-for-genomics-and-molecular-work-in-pulses/ |title=SHANTI SWARUP BHATNAGAR AWARD FOR GENOMICS AND MOLECULAR WORK IN PULSES |date=27 September 2016 |publisher=ICRISAT |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161028150943/http://www.icrisat.org/shanti-swarup-bhatnagar-award-for-genomics-and-molecular-work-in-pulses/ |archive-date=28 October 2016 }}</ref> for his contributions to physical sciences in 1980.<ref name="View Bhatnagar Awardees">{{cite web|url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/AwardeeList.aspx |title=View Bhatnagar Awardees |publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize |date=2016 |access-date=12 November 2016 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161016194310/http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/AwardeeList.aspx |archive-date=16 October 2016 }}</ref>{{Refn|group=note|Long link – please select award year to see details}}

== Biography ==
[[File:BARC nuclear reactor.JPG|thumb|235px|Bhabha Atomic Research Centre]]
N. S. Satya Murthy, who held a PhD from [[University of Bombay]] (1967), served as an assistant director at the [[Bhabha Atomic Research Centre]] and as the head of the Nuclear Physics Division of the institution.<ref name="Deceased fellow">{{Cite web|url=http://insaindia.res.in/detail/N81-0713 |title=Deceased fellow |date=2017 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170425205030/http://insaindia.res.in/detail/N81-0713 |archive-date=25 April 2017 }}</ref> His research was focused on [[Magnet|magnetic materials]] and his studies of the materials with the help of [[thermal neutrons]] have widened the understanding of the subject.<ref name="Brief Profile of the Awardee">{{Cite web |url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/Detail.aspx?AID=332 |title=Brief Profile of the Awardee |date=2017 |publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize |access-date=12 November 2016}}</ref> Murthy and his team were credited with the discovery of novel magnetic structures and a polarizer for thermal neutrons. His contributions have been reported in the design of neutron facilities of the [[Dhruva reactor]] and he led a group of scientists who conceptualized and fabricated several components of the [[Nuclear reactor|reactor]].<ref name="Deceased fellow" /> Murthy also contributed in developing [[superconducting magnet]]s at BARC and his work assisted in the development of ''Yafet-Kittel type of [[ferrimagnetism]]''.<ref name="Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners">{{cite web |url=http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf |title=Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners |publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research |date=1999 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304043957/http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf |archive-date=4 March 2016 |access-date=25 April 2017 }}</ref> His studies have been documented by way of a number of articles{{Refn|group=note|Please see ''Selected bibliography'' section}} and the article repository of the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] has listed 23 of them.<ref name="Browse by Fellow">{{Cite web|url=http://repository.ias.ac.in/view/fellows/Satya_Murthy=3ANivarthi_Suryanarayana=3A=3A.html |title=Browse by Fellow |date=2017 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170425115001/http://repository.ias.ac.in/view/fellows/Satya_Murthy%3D3ANivarthi_Suryanarayana%3D3A%3D3A.html |archive-date=25 April 2017 }}</ref> Besides, he published a monograph, ''Magnetism'', along with L. Madhav Rao<ref name="MurthyRao1985">{{cite book|author1=N. S. Satya Murthy |author2=L. Madhav Rao |title=Magnetism |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=A9rvAAAAMAAJ |year=1985 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170425122051/https://books.google.com/books?id=A9rvAAAAMAAJ |archive-date=25 April 2017 }}</ref> and his work has been cited by other scientists.<ref name="Honig2012">{{cite book|author=J Honig |title=Preparation and Characterization of Materials |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=KtNqVqclQKcC&pg=PA131 |date=2 December 2012 |publisher=Elsevier |isbn=978-0-323-14435-3 |pages=131– |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170425130853/https://books.google.com/books?id=KtNqVqclQKcC&pg=PA131 |archive-date=25 April 2017 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book|title=Indian Journal of Pure & Applied Physics |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=5WLyAAAAMAAJ |year=1992 |publisher=Council of Scientific & Industrial Research | isbn=9788185038964 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170425130840/https://books.google.com/books?id=5WLyAAAAMAAJ |archive-date=25 April 2017 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book|title=Proceedings of the Nuclear Physics and Solid State Physics Symposium |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=VLMZAAAAIAAJ |year=1975 |publisher=Department of Atomic Energy, Government of India. |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170425124302/https://books.google.com/books?id=VLMZAAAAIAAJ |archive-date=25 April 2017 }}</ref>

Murthy introduced such experimental techniques as the [[Compton edge|Compton profile spectroscopy]], [[Mossbauer spectroscopy]] and [[Raman spectroscopy]] at BARC and pioneered basic research on subjects like electron states, of cooperative effects and long wavelength [[Excitation (magnetic)|excitation]]s.<ref name="Deceased fellow" /> He contributed to the establishment of the [[Raja Ramanna Centre for Advanced Technology]] and was one of the founders of the Magnetics Society of India where he also served as the vice president. Murthy coordinated academic courses on ''Magnetism'' and ''Integrated Circuits'' for Indian Physics Association and was the general secretary of the organization for two terms from 1973 to 1977.<ref name="Executive Committees of IPA">{{Cite web |url=http://www.ipa1970.org.in/pastexlist.php |title=Executive Committees of IPA |date=2017 |publisher=Indian Physics Association |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170411060234/http://www.ipa1970.org.in/pastexlist.php |archive-date=11 April 2017 |access-date=25 April 2017 }}</ref> He was also an editorial board member of the [[Bulletin of Materials Science]].<ref name="Deceased fellow" />

Satya Murthy died on 8 October 1984, at the age of 48.<ref name="Fellow profile">{{Cite web|url=http://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Satya_Murthy,_Dr_Nivarthi_Suryanarayana |title=Fellow profile |date=2017 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170425120051/http://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Satya_Murthy%2C_Dr_Nivarthi_Suryanarayana |archive-date=25 April 2017 }}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
The [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] elected Murthy as a fellow in 1975.<ref name="Fellow profile" /> The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]], one of the highest Indian science awards in 1979.<ref name="CSIR list of Awardees">{{Cite web|url=http://www.csir.res.in/careeraward/prize-winner-indexdiscipline-wise |title=CSIR list of Awardees |date=2017 |publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170409021146/http://www.csir.res.in/careeraward/prize-winner-indexdiscipline-wise |archive-date=9 April 2017 }}</ref> He became an elected fellow of the [[Indian National Science Academy]] in 1981.<ref name="INSA Year Book 2016">{{Cite web |url=http://www.insaindia.res.in/pdf/YearBook_2016.pdf |title=INSA Year Book 2016 |date=2017 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161104001952/http://www.insaindia.res.in/pdf/YearBook_2016.pdf |archive-date=4 November 2016 |access-date=25 April 2017 }}</ref> He was also a life member of the Magnetics Society of India.<ref name="Deceased fellow" /> The Indian Physics Association has instituted an annual award, ''N. S. Satya Murthy Memorial Award'' for recognizing research excellence in physical sciences among young scientists.<ref name="N. S. Satya Murthy Memorial Award in Physics for Young Scientists">{{Cite web|url=http://www.ipa1970.org.in/nsabout.php |title=N. S. Satya Murthy Memorial Award in Physics for Young Scientists |date=2017 |publisher=Indian Physics Association |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170425122823/http://www.ipa1970.org.in/nsabout.php |archive-date=25 April 2017 }}</ref><ref name="Dr Sudarshan Ananth: NS Satya Murthy Memorial Award">{{Cite web|url=http://www.iiserpune.ac.in/news/dr-sudarshan-ananth-ns-satya-murthy-memorial-award |title=Dr Sudarshan Ananth: NS Satya Murthy Memorial Award |date=2017 |publisher=IISER Pune |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170425120634/http://www.iiserpune.ac.in/news/dr-sudarshan-ananth-ns-satya-murthy-memorial-award |archive-date=25 April 2017 }}</ref>
